newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak foreign trade gap widens on import surge.
newsitem.headline: Slovak foreign trade gap widens on import surge.

text.p: Slovakia's foreign trade gap widened in August, spurred by a rise in car imports, chemicals, mineral oils and aeroplanes, the Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said on Tuesday.

The SUSR said in a report that the trade deficit for the first eight months of the year widened to 35.3 billion crowns, from 31.89 billion for the January-July period, with slow export growth also a factor. The deficit was 561 million crowns in January-August last year.
Imports grew 24.8 percent year-on-year to 207 billion crowns, while exports were up by 3.9 percent to 172 billion.
The SUSR said about 35 billion crowns of imports comprised fossil fuels and mineral oils.
Imports for construction of the Mochovce nuclear power plant took up 31.8 billion crowns, while car imports totalled 18.5 billion crowns.

"The import volume was mainly influenced by higher imports of motor vehicles, aeroplanes and ships ... compared with the same period of last year," the SUSR said. "In decline were imports of animal and vegetable fats and oils."
The main export commodities were iron and rolled steel, accounting for 24.6 billion crowns in the eight month period.
The Czech Republic remained Slovakia's biggest trading partner, accounting for 31.8 percent of total exports and 25.4 percent of imports.
Germany and Austria held on to second and third places as importers of Slovak goods, with a 20.5 and 6.0 percent share of the country's total exports.
The second and third largest share of Slovakia's imports came from Russia and Germany, accounting for 18.4 and 14.5 percent respectively.
Trade with OECD countries produced a 10.83 billion crown deficit, while that with Russia was 32.23 billion in deficit.
Slovakia had a surplus of 9.0 billion crowns with the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) countries.
